recommendation.summary: S5 FD-passing process handoff with identity state transfer (new binary).
justification: dependency/toolchain/runtime/native/embedded change needs a new binary; S5 keeps the listening socket and transfers state unchanged (state schema identical)

goroutine-structure, long-running or start-up code changed: in-process patching would leave old code running in goroutines that never return; a new process starts the new goroutine structure, and the old one is drained and exits

S6 blockers (3): : language/toolchain version changed; github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/microservices-demo/src/frontend.main: main() runs once at start-up (never re-executed / never returns); github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/microservices-demo/src/frontend.frontendServer: layout of compiled-in type frontendServer changed (1 functions use it); S6 replaces functions, not types
alternatives: Kubernetes rolling update (loses in-memory state, needs surge capacity)
risks: new package-level variable github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/microservices-demo/src/frontend.assistantEnabled: under S6 it lives in the patch plugin and is re-initialised by every later patch generation
no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 8 functions
8 patched functions are in package main; a Go plugin cannot import package main, so hotpatchgen must relocate them into an importable package
type information is partial (411/418 type errors old/new; third-party packages are opaque): call-graph and state reachability are lower bounds
quiescence: old activations of main(), init-started or long-running goroutines never return, so the old process is retired by exit, not by draining; set a drain deadline in the S5 upgrader
toolchain changed: S2/S6 plugin delivery is impossible (plugins must match the host toolchain exactly); only a new process works
